If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture upward momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and forecast is trending upward, apply a 1–2% downward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, apply a 1–2% upward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid premature reversal.

In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment shifts from negative to positive, apply a 1–3% upward correction to reflect sentiment reversal momentum.

If sentiment remains consistently positive over 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast tail end (25–30 days) to reflect sustained bullish sentiment.
